discovery.title: Discovering dance and theatre
discovery.description: Before writing, bring the theme to life with the body: videos, music, worksheets and pictures to explore movement, improvisation and stage design.
discovery.ageNote: Resources suited to {{range}} year-olds, the age range chosen in step 1.

serpentineAnnabelle.title: Annabelle's serpentine dance
serpentineAnnabelle.description: One of the very first dance films (1894): the dancer swirls her dress like wings.
serpentineAnnabelle.activity: Watch the film, then each child takes a scarf and invents their own serpentine dance: spin, ripple, take flight.

serpentineLumiere.title: The dance of the veils
serpentineLumiere.description: A dancer filmed by the Lumière brothers creates shapes with large veils.
serpentineLumiere.activity: In pairs, one moves a piece of fabric and the other mirrors it with their whole body. Then swap roles.

animalWakeUp.title: Animal body warm-up
animalWakeUp.description: A step-by-step worksheet to warm up the class by moving like different animals.
animalWakeUp.activity: Follow the six steps of the worksheet, from the stretching cat to the resting tortoise.

blueDancers.title: Dancers' poses
blueDancers.description: Edgar Degas' Blue Dancers: observe the dancers' gestures and postures.
blueDancers.activity: Each child picks a dancer from the painting and copies her pose. The others guess which one.

pierrotMime.title: Pierrot's mime
pierrotMime.description: Pierrot, a theatre character painted by Watteau: telling a story without a word.
pierrotMime.activity: In silence, mime one of Pierrot's emotions (joy, surprise, sadness): the class has to recognise it.

livingStatues.title: Statues coming to life
livingStatues.description: Slow music (Erik Satie's Gymnopédie No. 1) for a drama improvisation exercise.
livingStatues.activity: The children are statues. While the music plays, they slowly come to life; when it stops, they freeze.

swanImprovisation.title: Dancing like a swan
swanImprovisation.description: The Swan by Camille Saint-Saëns, from The Carnival of the Animals.
swanImprovisation.activity: Listen to the music with your eyes closed, then dance the swan gliding on the water, with wide, gentle movements.

operaOrchestra.title: The orchestra musicians
operaOrchestra.description: Edgar Degas' The Orchestra at the Opera: the musicians who accompany the dance.
operaOrchestra.activity: Spot the instruments in the painting, then invent a body percussion rhythm to accompany a dance.

setDesign.title: Drawing a stage set
setDesign.description: A set design by Philippe Chaperon for the opera: columns, light and depth.
setDesign.activity: Draw the set for a scene of your tale, thinking about what is at the front, middle and back of the stage.

lightAndVeils.title: Light and costumes
lightAndVeils.description: How a simple piece of fabric and light turn the dancer's body into a landscape.
lightAndVeils.activity: With a torch and some fabric, look for shadows and shapes to use in your staging.

chambord.title: Château de Chambord
chambord.description: A majestic Renaissance castle, ideal as the setting for a king's palace.
chambord.reason: Its famous double-helix staircase and village-like rooftops inspire movements and encounters on stage.

montSaintMichel.title: Mont-Saint-Michel
montSaintMichel.description: An abbey perched on a rock, surrounded by the sea at high tide.
montSaintMichel.reason: A place between land and sea, perfect for imagining a crossing or a quest, and for dancing the movement of the tides.

broceliande.title: Brocéliande Forest
broceliande.description: The Paimpont forest, linked in legend to Merlin, the fairy Viviane and the Knights of the Round Table.
broceliande.reason: A legendary forest for mysterious encounters: trees and ferns become characters to dance.

kingArthur.title: King Arthur
kingArthur.description: The legendary king who pulled the sword from the stone and gathered the Knights of the Round Table.
kingArthur.reason: A central hero of medieval legends, who can be a fair king, a mentor or a hero on a quest.

joanOfArc.title: Joan of Arc
joanOfArc.description: A young girl from Lorraine who became a war leader and freed Orléans in 1429.
joanOfArc.reason: A brave historical figure, to talk about determination and dance the momentum of a group.

morganLeFay.title: Morgan le Fay
morganLeFay.description: A powerful sorceress of the Arthurian legends, sometimes an ally, sometimes an enemy.
morganLeFay.reason: A magical, ambiguous character who opens a discussion about allies and antagonists.

moulinGalette.title: Dance at the Moulin de la Galette
moulinGalette.description: A popular dance in Montmartre painted by Renoir: people dance in the sun with friends.
moulinGalette.reason: A neighbourhood party full of movement, to imagine the ball or the final celebration of the tale.

federationFestival.title: The Festival of the Federation
federationFestival.description: On 14 July 1790, a huge celebration brought crowds together on the Champ-de-Mars in Paris.
federationFestival.reason: A great historical gathering to work on crowd movements and group scenes.

degasDanceClass.title: The Dance Class
degasDanceClass.description: Edgar Degas paints the young dancers of the Opéra during a lesson.
degasDanceClass.reason: To observe classical dance postures and compare them with the class's own movements.

bayeuxTapestry.title: The Bayeux Tapestry
bayeuxTapestry.description: An embroidery nearly 70 metres long that tells a story in pictures, scene after scene.
bayeuxTapestry.reason: It splits a story into successive scenes, just like the danced tale: a model for your plot.

pierrotWatteau.title: Pierrot, by Watteau
pierrotWatteau.description: Pierrot, a character from Italian comedy, standing before the audience in his white costume.
pierrotWatteau.reason: A silent, expressive theatre character, to work on mime and wordless emotions.

redRidingHood.title: Little Red Riding Hood
redRidingHood.description: Charles Perrault's tale, illustrated by Gustave Doré.
redRidingHood.reason: A tale everyone knows, to spot the structure of a story and reinvent the meeting with the wolf.

pussInBoots.title: Puss in Boots
pussInBoots.description: A cunning cat helps his master become a marquis, in Perrault's tale illustrated by Doré.
pussInBoots.reason: A clever, energetic character, with a castle and an ogre: plenty to invent lively scenes.

cinderella.title: Cinderella
cinderella.description: Perrault's tale, from the palace ball to the glass slipper, illustrated by Doré.
cinderella.reason: A tale where dance is at the heart of the story: the ball scene can become a highlight of the show.
